clue.text: Cheap accommodation poet's always got in theatre

indicators.note: got in tells us one piece has been taken inside another

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A poet who is always in the theatre can only afford the cheapest lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger accommodation on a ship.

clue.text: Sea god cut short voyage to North

indicators.note: cut short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a voyage or journey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea god's voyage northward is curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology Triton is a sea deity, son of Poseidon, blowing a conch shell.

clue.text: Excuse for one who can't perform well in exams

definitions.text: Excuse for one who can't perform well in exams

parts.words: Excuse for one who can't perform well in exams
parts.note: reads like a jibe about a poor student, but means a formal certificate excusing a candidate too ill to sit examinations

explanation.surface: Someone always has an excuse for doing badly in exams.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'can't perform well' is literal illness, not lack of talent: British universities award this degree to students prevented by sickness from sitting finals.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegrotat is a university certificate or degree given to a student unable through illness to take exams.

clue.text: List fowl, omitting one from brace of ducks

indicators.note: omitting says some letters are left out of the word

parts.note: a rooster is a male domestic fowl
a duck is zero, O, in cricket scoring; a brace is two, so one of the pair is a single O

explanation.surface: A list of poultry where one of a pair of ducks has been left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'duck' is a cricket score of nought, so a brace of ducks is OO, and ROOSTER has one of those two letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster is a list, especially a rota of people's duties.

clue.text: Woodman finally cutting trees in order to make logs

indicators.note: cutting here means slicing into the middle of another group of letters
put in order means the letters of trees are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A lumberjack fells trees so he can produce logs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges TREES to ETERS, and N from Woodman cuts in after the first E. 'logs' is a verb, recording, not lumber.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data is to log or record it, so enters is synonymous with logs as a verb.

clue.text: Chap dramatically making serious pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is as it is said

parts.note: earnest means serious and sincere

explanation.surface: A man in a play makes a solemn declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Ernest Worthing in Oscar Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest, a comedy built on this very pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's name and the hero of Wilde's comedy, hence a chap on stage.

clue.text: Singers producing quite high notes in audition

indicators.note: audition here means hearing, so the phrase is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound banknotes, fairly high in value

explanation.surface: Singers at an audition hit some fairly high notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are banknotes, not musical ones: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenors are male singers with a high voice range.

clue.text: Rock thrower one can't keep off the grass?

definitions.text: one can't keep off the grass?
definitions.meaning: grass is slang for cannabis, so this is a habitual user of the drug

explanation.definitionFit: A stoner literally throws stones, and in slang is a habitual cannabis smoker.

clue.text: National Red Cross hero?

parts.note: suggests a humanitarian charity worker, but means the patron saint of England, whose emblem is a red cross on white

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure from a nation's Red Cross organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Cross charity is the false trail; the red cross on a white ground is England's flag, named for its patron saint, a dragon-slaying hero.
explanation.definitionFit: England's patron saint is honoured as the national hero whose cross forms the English flag.

clue.text: Be a consumer, but not seriously, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be taken as it sounds

parts.note: said in jest means said as a joke, not seriously

explanation.surface: Someone tells us they are only joking about being a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take in food or drink, i.e. to consume.

clue.text: Introduction of gas with a European helping

parts.note: a ration is an allotted portion or helping

explanation.surface: Gas is being brought in with some help from a European.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeration is the process of introducing air or another gas into a liquid or soil.

clue.text: Answer: area including south India

indicators.note: including says one pair of letters is put inside another

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quiz answer: the region that takes in southern India.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the continent is indeed an area that includes south India.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent covers a vast area that includes the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Main course, for example, that can't compete

definitions.meaning: a dish that is not the first course of a meal
someone or something with no chance of success

explanation.definitionFit: A main course is literally not a starter, and a non-starter is a hopeless candidate.

clue.text: Divisive policy contrived eg with iron gates

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An iron-gated barrier is put up to divide people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges EG plus IRON GATES; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Segregation is the policy of separating groups, typically by race, which divides society.

clue.text: Kind of servant one keeps

definitions.meaning: a household attendant of long standing in a family
something that holds things in place, such as a dental brace

explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving servant, and also any device or person that retains something.

clue.text: Musician's the first in orchestra breaking a string

indicators.note: the first in picks out the opening letter of the word
breaking means the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A player's first in the orchestra to break a string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first in orchestra' gives O; 'breaking' rearranges A STRING to RGANIST. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist is a musician who plays the organ.

clue.text: Object to being put in post, not for the first time

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
sent means posted, dispatched by mail

explanation.surface: Someone objects to being posted repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: '+ after' order: RE comes first in the answer although the clue gives it second.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitterness about it, effectively objecting to it.

clue.text: Wise man at Troy joins retreat with other ranks

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A sage at the Trojan war withdraws along with ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the aged, wise counsellor of the Greeks at the siege of Troy in Homer.

clue.text: They are felt to be very exciting people

definitions.meaning: people who cause a great stir, as in an overnight hit performer

explanation.definitionFit: Sensations are physical feelings, and a sensation is also a person causing great excitement.

clue.text: Writer from Western Europe

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An author who comes from the west of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy; he was born in Ireland, fitting the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist, author of Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Relation between staff nurse and matron

definitions.meaning: a female sibling, a family member
in British hospitals, the senior nurse rank above staff nurse and below matron

explanation.walkthrough: In UK hospitals a ward sister ranks above a staff nurse and below the matron.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a family relation and, in British hospitals, a senior nurse ranked between staff nurse and matron.

clue.text: Fast woman who leaves the rest behind?

definitions.meaning: slang for a sexually promiscuous woman
someone who departs, going on ahead

explanation.definitionFit: Goer is British slang for a promiscuous woman, and literally one who goes, departing.

clue.text: Frenchman has drink, German not following suit

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A Frenchman drinking with a German who won't follow the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following suit' is the card-game sense: to renege is to fail to play a card of the suit led.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, reneging means failing to follow suit when able to do so.

clue.text: Boy attending a musical performance

parts.note: a son is a boy child
at means present at, attending

explanation.surface: A boy goes along to a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition for performance by one or a few instruments.

clue.text: For example, future king is more nervous

parts.note: the future is an example of a grammatical tense
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An heir apparent is getting more jittery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'future king' looks like a crown prince; 'future' is a verb tense and the king is R.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenser is the comparative of tense, meaning more anxious or on edge.

clue.text: Performer involving second kind of muscle

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around another piece

parts.note: a tenor is a singer, a performer

explanation.surface: A singer's act features another type of muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tensor is a muscle that tightens or stretches a part of the body.
